summary: We built a free, public web tool that helps anyone see how a patch of sky changes over time in NASA's SPHEREx data. It shows real SPHEREx cutouts as a short animation, so moving or changing objects stand out. Because SPHEREx observes the same position at different wavelengths in different exposures, a brightness change between frames is not necessarily variability. To avoid misleading users, the tool only animates frames from the same detector and wavelength and never mixes bands. A citizen-science mode lets non-experts mark candidate movers, stars, variables and defects, and export their marks as CSV. The interface is available in English and Portuguese, and views can be shared by link. The live demo currently uses real SPHEREx DR1 images of WISE 0855; we never present simulated data as real. Data: SPHEREx DR1 via NASA/IPAC IRSA (DOI 10.26131/IRSA678).
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Our tool turns SPHEREx spectral images into a "blink" animation of a small patch of sky. The user picks a target, then chooses a detector and wavelength group. The tool plays the matching cutouts in time order, with controls for speed, zoom, crosshair, color palette and a difference view. A scale bar shows the field of view, and the current view can be shared by link. A citizen-science mode lets non-experts mark candidate movers, stars, variables and defects on the image and export their marks as a CSV file.

SCIENTIFIC RIGOR

SPHEREx sees one sky position at different wavelengths in different exposures. Brightness changes between frames of different bands are therefore not variability. Our viewer only animates frames from the same detector and the same wavelength. Each frame has its median subtracted, and all frames share one asinh stretch, so changes are comparable.

DATA AND TOOLS

Data: SPHEREx DR1 spectral images from NASA/IPAC IRSA (TAP, SIA2 and the cutout service). Python (astropy, pyvo) for querying and downloading cutouts, with retries and caching. Front end: React, Vite and Material UI, as a static site with WebP frames, hosted on Cloudflare. The interface is available in English and Portuguese.

INTENDED IMPACT

Make SPHEREx data approachable for the public, students and educators, and give citizen scientists a way to flag candidate moving or varying objects for experts to check.

CREATIVITY

We designed the tool around the main scientific pitfall of SPHEREx data, mixing bands, instead of hiding it. We also added a classification mode so that non-experts can contribute.

LIMITATIONS (HONEST SCOPE)

The live demo currently contains real images for one target, WISE 0855. During development the IRSA services returned repeated 502 errors, so we did not publish other targets without verified real data. We did not use simulated data in the tool. Users' marks are stored locally in the browser and are exported as CSV. The site uses pre-processed data, so it does not yet accept arbitrary coordinates.

ACKNOWLEDGEMENT AND CITATION

This publication makes use of data products from the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), which is a joint project of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the California Institute of Technology, and is funded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

SPHEREx DR1 spectral images: DOI 10.26131/IRSA678.
